subject: mouth breathing
title: What If You Only Breathed Through Your Mouth?

scenes.text: What if you only ever breathed through your mouth? Your lungs aren't the first thing to suffer.
You breathe about ten to fifteen thousand litres of air a day. Your nose warms it to about thirty-four degrees first.
It also brings that air to about ninety percent humidity. Mouth breathing skips both steps.
By morning your mouth dries out. In one sleep study, mouth breathing dropped mouth pH as low as three point six.
Tooth enamel starts dissolving below pH five point five. So all night, every night, your teeth sit in acid.
You'd also miss nitric oxide, a gas your sinuses make that reaches your lungs only through your nose.

description:
What if you only breathed through your mouth? We breathe about 10,000 to 15,000 litres of air a day, and the nose warms it to about 34 degrees C and roughly 90% humidity before it reaches the lungs.
In a University of Otago sleep study, forced mouth breathing dropped mouth pH as low as 3.6, well below the 5.5 at which enamel begins to dissolve. Nasal breathing also carries nitric oxide made in the sinuses down to the lungs.
What should we run through next?
